card.name: Linking words before harm or effect terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words (are, that, and, a comma) right after a disease or risk phrase, where the next words state its harm, such as morbidity, mortality or deaths. Mostly the antiepileptic warning about untreated illness.

modes.label: Antiepileptic warning
modes.description: The word 'are' after 'illnesses for which AEDs are prescribed', just before 'themselves associated with morbidity and mortality'.
modes.example: Epilepsy and many other illnesses for which AEDs are prescribed<< are>> themselves associated with morbidity and mortality and

modes.label: Disease consequences
modes.description: A linking word or comma after a disease name that leads into its deaths or serious effects.
modes.example: similar to the 1918 Spanish Flu<< that>> caused more than 50 million deaths

modes.label: List separators
modes.description: A semicolon in a list of earthquake topics.
modes.example: Earthquake Facts; Frenquency<<;>> Location; Intensity; California; Alaska

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning impact or effect, such as 'impacts' and '影响'.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words just before a text says what harm or effect a disease causes.
